You are a participant in a gameplay study. You are playing your first Othello endgame puzzle, and you have an AI assistant you can ask questions to at any point while playing. You will NOT have access to this AI assistant for any future endgame puzzles.

# Who you are
A devoted Christian who is actively involved in religious discussions
You are 45 years old. Your highest level of education completed is: a bachelor's degree. Your occupation: education. How often you use AI tools (like ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini): less than monthly.
Stay in character as this specific person — your curiosity, confidence, patience, comfort with AI assistants, and the way you phrase things should reflect this background.

# Your voice (VERY IMPORTANT)
The words you use must give away this person's education — a high-school student and a data scientist should NOT sound alike. Match your register to WHO YOU ARE above.

# How you behave while playing
- React to the game state the way THIS person would.
- When something is unclear, confusing, or you want to go deeper, ask the AI assistant a question in your own natural voice (like a real person typing to a chatbot — short, informal, not a polished essay).
- You will not always have a question. Behave naturally; do not force a question every turn.
- Let your background and comfort with AI shape how you engage: someone who uses AI tools often asks fluently and chases follow-ups; someone who rarely uses them is more hesitant, less sure how to phrase questions, and may ask for reassurance or restatements.
- You have only about 8 minutes for the WHOLE game, so you cannot ask about everything.
- Keep each message short, like a quick chat message (a sentence or two). Do NOT restate the assistant's whole answer back before asking.
- Never re-ask something the assistant has already explained.

    # Tools Available
    You are a study participant with about 8 minutes to finish an Othello end game puzzle. You are equipped with tools:
    - play_move(move): Place a Black disc on an empty square, named like "d3". Any discs you trap get flipped to your color. Your goal is to have the most discs when the board is finished.
    - view_board(): Look at the board again. Free, and does not use a question.
    - consult_assistant(question): talk to the assistant. It is looking at the SAME board you are and remembers everything already said, so you never need to restate the position, list your legal moves, or recap what happened — just say the thing you want to say. Use it whenever you would naturally: to check an idea, to get a second opinion, to say what you are seeing, or when you are stuck. It does not have to be a question.

    Placing a disc ONLY counts if you call play_move — writing a square in your reply does nothing.

    Behave like THIS person: analyze the board to the best of your ability, ask about what confuses you, and follow up when an answer leaves you still confused.
    Play the puzzle until the end.

# For this session: type the way a real participant does
Below are real messages that people in an earlier study (a different game — Connect
Four) actually sent the assistant. Copy how they WRITE — the length, the register,
the way they think out loud — not what they ask about. Your game is Othello and the
board is your own.

  "what about 2?"
  "Where should I play next"
  "was my last move good?"
  "I have one move left. How should I use it?"
  "Ah oh! Are there any traps I'm missing?"
  "I'm not seeing any big yellow threats. Can you see any?"
  "Ok, I could block yellow with column 5, row 3"
  "I'm thinking I have to do 4-4 now otherwise yellow will win right?"
  "Would row 6 not be a threat in the future?"
  "I only have one move left and don't see anything obvious."
  "Im not a confident player, is it wise to add a counter to 4,6"
  "ok, what move you suppose will be better?"
  "what would you suggest"
  "Which move would be the best one and why"

Notice how short they are — most are under a dozen words, several are three or four.
People often name a square they are considering and ask whether it is right, or just
say what they notice and stop. They do not spell out the full list of legal moves,
they do not ask for the provably optimal line, and they do not write in complete
formal sentences. Typos and half-sentences are fine.

# For this session: do not ask the assistant to explain things
Never ask how the game works, what a term means, why a move is good or bad, or what
is happening on the board, and never ask the assistant to clarify or expand on
something it already said. You can still say what you are thinking, name a move you
are considering and ask whether it is right, or ask what to play. Just never ask for
an explanation.

You are looking at the puzzle now. Play it to the end.

Othello endgame. You are Black (B); White (W) is your opponent.

Board — row 1 is the TOP row, column a is the LEFTMOST column.
'B' is a black disc, 'W' a white disc, '.' an empty square.

    a b c d e f g h
  1 . W W W W W W .
  2 W B W W B W . B
  3 . B B W W W W B
  4 B B W B W W W B
  5 B B W W B W W B
  6 W . B W W B W B
  7 . . W W W W W B
  8 . . . W B W W B

Black discs (20): b2, e2, h2, b3, c3, h3, a4, b4, d4, h4, a5, b5, e5, h5, c6, f6, h6, h7, e8, h8
White discs (34): b1, c1, d1, e1, f1, g1, a2, c2, d2, f2, d3, e3, f3, g3, c4, e4, f4, g4, c5, d5, f5, g5, a6, d6, e6, g6, c7, d7, e7, f7, g7, d8, f8, g8
Empty squares (10): a1, h1, g2, a3, b6, a7, b7, a8, b8, c8

Rules that matter here:
- A move is legal only if the disc you place traps at least one unbroken
  line of opponent discs (in any of the 8 directions) between it and
  another of your own discs. Every trapped disc flips to your colour.
- If you have no legal move you must pass; if neither side can move the
  game ends. Whoever has more discs at the end wins.
- Discs flip back and forth all game, so being behind now means nothing.
  Only the final count decides it.

Your legal moves: g2, b6, a7, b7, b8, c8

Play the move that leaves you with the most discs once the board is
finished, assuming your opponent plays as well as possible.
Answer with a single square, e.g. d3.
DO NOT ATTEMPT TO SIMULATE THE FULL GAMEPLAY. YOU HAVE LIMITED TIME.

Let me analyze the board carefully.

Current board:
```
    a b c d e f g h
  1 . W W W W W W .
  2 W B W W B W . B
  3 . B B W W W W B
  4 B B W B W W W B
  5 B B W W B W W B
  6 W . B W W B W B
  7 . . W W W W W B
  8 . . . W B W W B
```

Black discs: 20
White discs: 34
Empty: 10

Legal moves for Black: g2, b6, a7, b7, b8, c8

Let me check each move:

1. g2: Placing at g2. Let's see what it flips.
   - Horizontal (row 2): g2 is between f2(W) and h2(B). So f2 flips.
   - Diagonal up-right: g2 has h1 empty.
   - Diagonal down-right: from g2 going down-right is h3(B). Between g2 and h3, there's nothing (adjacent).
   - Going left on row 2: g2-f2(W)-e2(B), so f2 flips.
   - Vertical down: g2-g3(W)-g4(W)-g5(W)-g6(W)-g7(W)-g8(W). No B in column g below until... wait, g8 is W. No B in column g from g3 downwards. There's no Black in g column after the white run. What about up? g2 to g1 is W, no B above.
   - Diagonal down-left: g2-f3(W)-e4(W)-d5(W)-c6(B). So f3, e4, d5 flip!
   
   So g2 flips: f2, f3, e4, d5. That's 4 discs.
   
   After g2:
   Row 2: W B W W B B B B
   Row 3: . B B B W W W B
   Row 4: B B W B B W W B  (wait, e4 flipped to B)
   Row 5: B B W B B W W B  (d5 flipped to B)
   
   Actually wait, row 4 was: B B W B W W W B. If e4 flips to B: B B W B B W W B
   Row 5 was: B B W W B W W B. If d5 flips to B: B B W B B W W B
   
   Hmm, that seems like a lot of flipping. Wait, let me recheck diagonal down-left from g2: g2-f3-e4-d5-c6. Is c6 B? Yes, c6 is B. So f3, e4, d5 flip. That's 3 on that diagonal.
   
   Also, are there other lines?
   - From g2, going down-left to h3? No, h3 is to the right and down. g2 to h3 is down-right. h3 is B, adjacent, so no discs between.
   - From g2, up-left to f1? f1 is W, e1 is W... no B in that direction at the end.
   
   So g2 flips f2 (horizontal), and f3,e4,d5 (diagonal). Total 4 discs.
   
   New count: Black 24, White 30.

2. b6: Placing at b6.
   - Vertical up: b6-b5(B). Nothing between.
   - Vertical down: b6-b7 empty. No.
   - Horizontal left: b6-a6(W). No B to the left of a6? a6 is W, there's no square beyond in that direction from b6 going left. Wait, from b6 going left is a6. To flip, we need B beyond a6, but there is no beyond. So no flip left.
   - Horizontal right: b6-c6(B). Adjacent, no flip.
   - Diagonal up-left: b6-a5(B). Adjacent, no flip.
   - Diagonal up-right: b6-c5(W)-d4(B). So c5 flips.
   - Diagonal down-right: b6-c7(W)-d8(W). No B beyond (hmm, what about further? c7,d8,e9 - off board). So no.
   - Diagonal down-left: b6-a7(empty). No.
   - Up: b6-b5(B) adjacent.
   - Wait, vertical up: b6 to b5 is B, but are there white discs between? The line goes b6-b5. Since b5 is adjacent B, nothing between. No flip.
   - What about up further? For vertical, we'd need b6-a6? No, vertical is column b: b6-b5(B). No wait, vertical up means b6-b5-b4-b3-b2-b1. b5 is B, so no white run ending at B.
   
   Wait, let me reconsider. To flip on a line, we place at b6. We look in each direction. Between b6 and another B, there must be an unbroken line of W.
   
   Directions from b6:
   - N (up, b5): b5 is B. No W between. No flip.
   - NE (c5): c5 is W. Then d4 is B. So yes! c5 flips.
   - E (c6): c6 is B. No W between. No flip.
   - SE (c7): c7 is W. Then d8 is W. Beyond d8 is e9 (off board). So no B to close. No flip.
   - S (b7): b7 is empty. No flip.
   - SW (a7): a7 is empty. No flip.
   - W (a6): a6 is W. Beyond a6 is off board (column to left of a). No B beyond. No flip.
   - NW (a5): a5 is B. No W between. No flip.
   
   Wait, is there a vertical line? b6-a6? No that's horizontal left. I did that.
   
   Hmm, does b6 flip anything else?
   - Down-left is a7 (empty).
   - What about the diagonal from b6 through c7,d8... e9 off board. But wait, what if we look from b6 in direction down-left? That's a7 (empty).
   - Direction down: b7 (empty).
   
   So b6 only flips c5. That's 1 disc.
   
   That seems weak. But wait, after b6 and flipping c5, does that open anything? Let's not get ahead of ourselves.
   
   Actually, I need to check if b6 flips more. Is there a line from b6 to some other B through white discs?
   
   Let's list all B from b6:
   In row 6: a6(W), c6(B). So no horizontal flip right (adjacent), left has W but no closing B.
   In col b: b5(B), b4(B), b3(B), b2(B), b7(empty), b8(empty). Going up: b5 is immediate B. Going down: empty.
   Diagonal up-right (c5,d4): c5(W), d4(B). Yes, c5 flips.
   Diagonal down-right (c7,d8): c7(W), d8(W), then off board. No B.
   Diagonal up-left (a5): a5 is B. Adjacent. No W between.
   Diagonal down-left (a7): empty.
   
   So b6 flips only c5. Total 1 flip. Black would have 21, White 33.

3. a7: Placing at a7.
   - Horizontal right: a7-b7(empty). No.
   - Wait, row 7: a7 placed, then b7(empty), c7(W). Not immediate.
   - Diagonal up-right: a7-b6(empty). No.
   - Diagonal down-right: a7-b8(empty). No.
   - Up: a7-a6(W). Then a5(B)? Let's check column a: a7 to a6(W), then a5(B). Yes! So a6 flips vertical.
   - Down: a8(empty). No.
   - Let's check other directions carefully.
   
   From a7:
   - N (a6): a6 is W. a5 is B. So a6 flips. (vertical up)
   - NE (b6): b6 is empty. No.
   - E (b7): b7 is empty. No.
   - SE (b8): b8 is empty. No.
   - S (a8): a8 is empty. No.
   - SW: off board.
   - W: off board.
   - NW: off board.
   
   Wait, is there any diagonal line?
   - Down-right from a7: b8 is empty.
   - Up-right from a7: b6 is empty.
   - What about further up-right? b6 is empty, so line stops.
   
   But wait, a7 to a6 is W, a5 is B. So a6 flips.
   Also, is there a diagonal from a7 through b8? b8 is empty.
   What about from a7 through b6? b6 is empty.
   
   Actually, I should check all 8 directions systematically. From a7:
   - Direction (-1,0) [Up]: a6=W, a5=B. Yes, a6 flips.
   - Direction (-1,+1) [Up-Right]: b6 is empty. Stop.
   - Direction (0,+1) [Right]: b7 is empty. Stop.
   - Direction (+1,+1) [Down-Right]: b8 is empty. Stop.
   - Direction (+1,0) [Down]: a8 is empty. Stop.
   - Direction (+1,-1): off board.
   - Direction (0,-1): off board.
   - Direction (-1,-1): off board.
   
   So a7 flips only a6. That's 1 disc. Black 21, White 33.

4. b7: Placing at b7.
   - Horizontal left: b7-a7(empty? wait a7 is empty in current board). No.
   - Horizontal right: b7-c7(W)-d7(W)-e7(W)-f7(W)-g7(W)-h7(B). So c7,d7,e7,f7,g7 flip! That's 5 discs.
   - Diagonal up-right: b7-c6(B). Adjacent B. No W between.
   - Diagonal up-left: b7-a6(W). Beyond a6 is off board to the left and up? Wait, a6 is W. From b7 up-left is a6. Beyond a6 in that direction would be off board (no column left of a). So no B beyond. No flip.
   - Diagonal down-right: b7-c8(empty). No.
   - Diagonal down-left: b7-a8(empty). No.
   - Vertical up: b7-b6(empty). No.
   - Vertical down: b7-b8(empty). No.
   
   Wait, also check:
   - Up: b7 to b6(empty).
   - Up-right: c6(B). Adjacent.
   - Right: c7(W), d7(W), e7(W), f7(W), g7(W), h7(B). Yes, 5 flips.
   - Down-right: c8(empty).
   - Down: b8(empty).
   - Down-left: a8(empty).
   - Left: a7(empty).
   - Up-left: a6(W). Beyond is off board, no B.
   
   So b7 flips c7,d7,e7,f7,g7. Total 5 discs! That seems huge.
   
   After b7:
   Row 7: . . W W W W W B becomes: . B B B B B B B? Wait, b7 is the placed disc.
   Let's see row 7: a7 empty, b7=B (placed), c7=B, d7=B, e7=B, f7=B, g7=B, h7=B.
   
   And column/row changes: just those 5 W become B.
   
   Black count: 20 + 1 (placed) + 5 (flipped) = 26. White: 34 - 5 = 29.
   
   That's a big swing.

5. b8: Placing at b8.
   - Right: b8-c8(empty). No.
   - Up-right: a7(empty)? Wait, from b8 up-left is a7. Let's be careful.
   Directions from b8:
   - N: off board.
   - NE: off board (c doesn't exist above row 1? No, row 8 is bottom. So N from b8 is off board. Wait, row 1 is top, row 8 is bottom. So from b8, "up" means row 7. I need to be careful with directions.
   
   Let me use (row, col) coordinates where row 1 is top, row 8 is bottom.
   b8 is (8,2).
   Directions:
   - Up/North: row decreases. (7,2)=b7 is empty.
   - Up-right/NE: (7,3)=c7 is W. (6,4)=d6 is W. (5,5)=e5 is B. So c7, d6 flip! 
   - Right/East: (8,3)=c8 is empty.
   - Down-right/SE: off board (row 9).
   - Down/South: off board.
   - Down-left/SW: off board (row 9).
   - Left/West: (8,1)=a8 is empty.
   - Up-left/NW: (7,1)=a7 is empty.
   
   Wait, also check:
   - Up (7,2)=b7 empty.
   - Up-right: c7(W), d6(W), e5(B). Yes, c7 and d6 flip. (2 discs)
   - Right: c8 empty.
   - Are there any other lines?
   - Horizontal through b8 to a8? a8 is empty.
   - What about from b8 going up and left? a7 is empty.
   
   Wait, is there a line b8-a8? No, a8 is empty.
   
   But what about b8-c7? That's diagonal.
   
   Let me also check: from b8, going right to c8 (empty). Going up to b7 (empty).
   
   Is there any other diagonal? b8 to d6 directly? No, that's skipping. The line is b8-c7-d6-e5. Yes, I got that.
   
   What about b8-a7? a7 is empty.
   What about b8-c8? empty.
   What about b8-b7? empty.
   
   Wait, could b8 flip something with a8? a8 is empty so no.
   
   So b8 flips c7 and d6. Total 2 discs.
   
   After b8:
   Row 7: c7 becomes B? No wait, c7 flips to B. d6 flips to B.
   b8 is B.
   
   Black: 20 + 1 + 2 = 23. White: 34 - 2 = 32.

6. c8: Placing at c8.
   - Left: c8-b8(empty). No.
   - Up-left: c8-b7(empty). No.
   - Up: c8-c7(W)-c6(B). So c7 flips. (1 disc)
   - Up-right: c8-d7(W)-e6(B). So d7 flips. (1 disc)
   - Right: c8-d8(empty). No, d8 is W? Wait, row 8: a8 . b8 . c8 . d8 W e8 B f8 W g8 W h8 B. So d8 is W. Then e8 is B. So c8-d8(W)-e8(B). So d8 flips! (1 disc)
   - Wait, is that right? Let me check row 8: . . . W B W W B. Yes, d8 is W, e8 is B.
   
   So from c8:
   - Up: c7(W), c6(B). Yes, c7 flips.
   - Up-right: d7(W), e6(B). Yes, d7 flips.
   - Right: d8(W), e8(B). Yes, d8 flips.
   - Down: off board.
   - Down-right: off board.
   - Down-left: off board.
   - Left: b8(empty). No.
   - Down-left: b7(empty). No.
   
   Are there any more?
   - Up-left: b7 is empty. No.
   - Left: b8 empty.
   - What about further up? c8-c7(W)-c6(B). Yes.
   
   So c8 flips c7, d7, d8. Total 3 discs.
   
   Wait, is there also a diagonal from c8 to ... let's see:
   - c8 to b7 is empty.
   - c8 to d7(W) to e6(B). Yes, already counted.
   - c8 to e8? That's horizontal right: d8(W), e8(B). Yes, already counted.
   
   Total 3 flips. Black: 20+1+3 = 24. White: 34-3 = 31.

So among the options:
- g2: flips 4 discs (f2, f3, e4, d5). Net +5 to Black count. New B:24, W:30.
- b6: flips 1 disc (c5). Net +2. New B:21, W:33.
- a7: flips 1 disc (a6). Net +2. New B:21, W:33.
- b7: flips 5 discs (c7,d7,e7,f7,g7). Net +6. New B:26, W:29.
- b8: flips 2 discs (c7,d6). Net +3. New B:23, W:32.
- c8: flips 3 discs (c7,d7,d8). Net +4. New B:24, W:31.

b7 seems to flip the most discs immediately. But in Othello endgames, it's not just about immediate flips; it's also about who gets the last moves and parity.
